rendered: The paper reports separate pairs of limonene and nerolidol titers, belonging to different engineering stages, plus a table entry for each compound.Lower pair — the universal terpenoid platform strain built by site-specific multicopy integration of the MVA pathway and terpene synthase genes:[1][2]with limonene and nerolidol reaching 14.12 g L^(cid:0) 1 and 32.33 g L^(cid:0) 1, respectively, in 5-L bioreactors.[3]Higher pair — the best engineered strains described in the heterologous-products section:limonene reached 22.8 g L^(cid:0) 1 (highest reported) [21][4](E)-Nerolidol reached 70.50 g L^(cid:0) 1 [24][5]These higher values are exactly the ones tabulated in Table 2[6], whose titer column is in mg per litre: 22,800[7] for (S)-limonene[8] (strain HBQA7 → LSF6[9]) and 70,500[10] for (E)-nerolidol[11] (strain HBQA7 → LN62[12]), both in fed-batch[13] mode. Converted to grams per litre these are 22.8[14] and 70.5[15] g per litre, i.e. identical to the running text. Checking both text values against the table's titer column confirms that each matches a tabulated entry after the unit conversion (count of agreeing entries):2[16] The nerolidol value is also repeated, unchanged, in the introduction's list of maximum terpenoid titers:Maximum titers of 70.50, 60.32, and 102.3 g L^(cid:0) 1 have been reported for (E)-nerolidol[17] Limonene is not named in that introductory list, and the table carries only the best fed-batch entry per product, so the earlier platform-strain results sit below the tabulated ones: the gap is[18]8.68[19] g per litre for limonene and38.17[20] g per litre for nerolidol. So the reported numbers are mutually consistent rather than contradictory: the table and the introduction agree with the section text on the best titers, while the section text additionally reports the earlier, lower platform-strain results. The only tension is in the wording of that earlier sentence, which introduces the result as shake-flask biosynthesis yet attributes the titers to bioreactor cultivation.[21][22]
